summary: Backend-only verification that the GLP trusted proxy (/api/glp/*) connectivity bug (sg-captcha 202) is fixed. All 3 non-destructive checks PASS against the external preview URL (EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://apeps-mobile-demo.preview.emergentagent.com): (1) GET /api/glp/health -> HTTP 200 JSON {ok:true, secret_configured:true, glp_base_url:'https://ap3p-fitness.com', upstream_reachable:true, upstream_status:200} and no secret leakage in the body. (2) POST /api/glp/auth/session with {username:'nobody@example.com', password:'wrongpass'} -> HTTP 401 application/json {"error":"invalid_credentials"} — upstream error cleanly proxied, no 500/crash, no sg-captcha. (3) GET /api/glp/crypto/networks with NO Authorization header -> HTTP 401 application/json {"code":"glp_unauthorized","message":"Unauthorized","data":{"status":401}} — unauthenticated request correctly surfaces upstream 401 (not 5xx, not 503 bot-block). The X-GLP-App-Secret header is server-side only in /app/backend/.env and is never echoed in any response. No destructive endpoints were touched (no /auth/register, no POST /orders).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/glp_proxy.py: User-Agent set to 'AP3P-Storefront-API/1.0' and GLP_BASE_URL='https://ap3p-fitness.com' with X-GLP-App-Secret header — matches the fix spec and resolves the SiteGround sg-captcha 202 regression.
backend/glp_proxy.py:_forward() has defense-in-depth: detects sg-captcha HTML and converts it to a traceable 503 upstream_blocked error (not a silent 200 with HTML body) — good observability.
backend/glp_proxy.py:_secret() short-circuits to 503 proxy_unconfigured when the shared secret is missing — prevents accidental anonymous calls to the connector.
backend/glp_proxy.py: Authorization: Bearer <token> is correctly rewritten to X-GLP-Customer-Token upstream; the client never needs to know the shared secret.
backend/.env: GLP_APP_SHARED_SECRET is server-side only; it is not present in /app/frontend/.env and is not echoed by /api/glp/health (verified by test_health_does_not_leak_secret).
No-store cache-control is set on all proxied responses — correct for authenticated and invoice reads.

rca_of_issue: Original symptom: every /api/glp/* call returned HTTP 202 with a SiteGround 'sg-captcha' HTML challenge body, blocking all connectivity. Root cause: the proxy was previously sending a browser-mimicking User-Agent and/or hitting the wrong host; SiteGround's AntiBot layer refused non-browser traffic that looked like a disguised browser. Mitigation (applied by main agent, verified here): (a) User-Agent switched to a dedicated server-to-server identifier 'AP3P-Storefront-API/1.0'; (b) GLP_BASE_URL aligned to https://ap3p-fitness.com; (c) GLP_APP_SHARED_SECRET aligned with the WordPress plugin. Verification: /api/glp/health returns upstream_status=200 (no HTML, no 202), /auth/session surfaces a real 401 JSON from WordPress, and /crypto/networks surfaces a real 401 JSON from the WordPress connector — all three indicate the sg-captcha challenge is no longer served and the proxy transparently forwards upstream responses.
